column1: # Body inventory for the next transcriptions: recovered VA, the arm that installs
# it, and how many absolute operands it reads (each one is a published slot the
# arm must set before it installs). Measured with tools/verify_bodies.py and the
# reference sources; not a proof, a work list.
# name                          recovered VA  arm key                        slots
# EmissiveLerpFix - BLOCKED on operand semantics, do not transcribe yet.
# The shim at 0x1001AF60 reads/writes five absolute operands (0x10159CC0,
# addresses out of the original file gives bytes that decode as code, not as a
# scratch block (d8 30 17 31 ba 31 da 31 19 32 bc 32 dc 32 1b 33 at 0x10159CC0),
# so either the operand addresses are not data (a store into code, which would be
# the original's own fault) or the body was read from a different section layout
# than the file has. Both readings change what has to be published, and a wrong
# guess produces a body that faults on the first call - so the key stays open
# until the operands are re-derived from the disassembly rather than assumed.
